criteria.evidence: Run in a scratch worktree (now removed). At ceb37b4a, TmrContentFontScaleTest (12 tests), TmrSectionLabelTest and TmrContentContrastTest all pass. Then only TmrFitText.kt was replaced with the b007a8c7 body: the state-in-onTextLayout shrink, step 0.92 and readAs. Shared helpers were imported from component, and TmrFitTextLayoutKey was declared but never set, so textLayouts() falls back to GetTextLayoutResult. Exactly 2 tests failed. firstFrameAtFontScale200ShowsNoSplitWord fails with AssertionError: the first frame lays out at the start size and splits the word. widerContainerLetsTheNameGrowBack fails with 'name did not grow back: 7.6982846 -> 7.6982846', because the remember key has no constraints. fileNameWithoutSeparatorsShrinksToTheFloorInsteadOfBreaking passes on both versions, as expected: it checks the settled state. Both new tests are true red-green tests for the r2 medium finding.

The diff has no PNG. 'No baseline changed' is plausible. At fontScale 1.0, autoSize is null. softWrap=true, maxLines=Int.MAX_VALUE and overflow=Clip equal the material3 Text defaults. The ZWSP text is unchanged, and semantics do not draw. So content_filecard_prototype_dark renders identically, and Screenshot tests pass in CI on the head. No font-200 file card baseline exists. Only content_listrow_font200 and content_progress_font200 do. I am not raising this as a finding. The font-200 file card behaviour is now pinned by four compose tests: no split on the first frame, start/2 <= fitted < start, no split when settled, and growth on a wider width. A pixel baseline would only add a lock on glyph rendering, and content_filecard already covers that at 1x with ZWSP breaks.

WholeWordAutoSize matches #307 (0205f503 chrome/TmrChromeText.kt): same getFontSize loop, SHRINK_STEP 0.9f, floor clamp, equals and hashCode. The differences are: (a) visibility and package: internal in component, not private in chrome; (b) the predicate. breaksInsideWord(layout) adds a bounds guard `end in 1 until text.length` and treats ZWSP and '-' as break boundaries before the line end. #307's splitsWord only treats whitespace as a boundary. getLineEnd(line) defaults to visibleEnd=false, so that call is the same. (c) The shared file also exports readAs and withBreakOpportunities, which #307 does not use. Kotlin has no unused-internal warning, so allWarningsAsErrors is not affected. Effect on chrome labels: the step labels ('Profile', 'Job', 'Tailor', '✓ %1$s', '%1$d %2$s') and tab labels ('Applications', 'Profile') contain no '-' or ZWSP. TmrTopBar titles come from callers, and at 0205f503 only tests call it, with no hyphenated titles. So no chrome label behaves differently today. A future hyphenated TopBar title could wrap after the '-' instead of shrinking further, which matches D40. Adoption steps: add the file byte-identical. Delete SHRINK_STEP, splitsWord and the private WholeWordAutoSize from TmrChromeText.kt. Import com.tailormyresume.core.designsystem.component.WholeWordAutoSize. Drop the now-unused imports TextAutoSize, TextAutoSizeLayoutScope, Constraints and TextUnit, and keep sp and TextLayoutResult. TmrCapsText's own semantics (clearAndSetSemantics with getTextLayoutResult forwarding) can stay as they are.

TmrFitText has a single caller, the TmrFileCard name inside a plain Column (TmrFileCard.kt:71). The Text has no children. clearAndSetSemantics drops only Text's own default properties: GetTextLayoutResult (now exposed as TmrFitTextLayoutKey, which r2 low 4 asked for) and the text-substitution actions. TmrSectionLabel: readAs(text) sits before semantics { heading() }. TmrSectionLabelTest proves the unmerged node has the text 'Tailored resumes' with Heading defined.

The new pairs match what the components draw: the paper badge is lime on an ink circle (TmrResumePaper.kt:91,100).
